title: Isandro and the Signal
premise: Ines Oyelaran, a clone of a murdered investigator, tends the derelict beacon at Station Vesper-9, the only post nobody else wanted. When a ship that officially never flew docks carrying a manifest with one impossible name — Isandro, her original's presumed killer — she discovers the massacre aboard it was erased from every fleet record to protect a fragile truce. As Ines and Isandro reconstruct the crime from fragments, salvage, and living memory, they uncover that the truce itself was purchased with the victims' silence. To end the cycle, Ines must broadcast the truth on her forgotten beacon before the truce expires, choosing justice over the law and a found family over the duty written into her genes.
about_author: Tamsin Okonkwo is a former maritime radio operator who spent six years listening to frequencies no one answered before turning to fiction. She writes from a converted signal station on the Atlantic coast, where she still keeps a beacon light burning out of principle.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. She maintains Vesper-9's ancient beacon, logging routine traffic in a station built for a war that ended without records. A quiet portrait of loneliness and inherited purpose; she talks to the ghost of her original through old case notes. Emotional beat: contentment fraying into doubt about who she is when the work is done.

chapters.title: A Ship That Never Flew
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The freighter Coriander docks unannounced, its registry matching a vessel destroyed eleven years ago. Its manifest lists one name too many: Isandro Reyes. Ines hides instead of hailing, heart pounding as footsteps echo in corridors that should be empty. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into the first thrill of purpose she has felt in years.

chapters.title: Isandro
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. She confronts the stowaway — not the monster from her original's case files but a gaunt man in his fifties who claims he was a witness, not a killer. He shows her a burned data shard the official record says never existed. Emotional beat: suspicion warring with recognition, two people shaped by the same dead woman.

chapters.title: Eleven Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. He recounts the Calypso Reach massacre: three hundred colonists gassed during a fleet 'quarantine,' then struck from every archive to preserve the ceasefire with the Meridian Compact. He has spent a decade running. Emotional beat: grief delivered flatly, more devastating for its restraint.

chapters.title: What the Clone Remembers
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Searching her original's sealed effects, Ines finds evidence the investigator died pursuing this same case — and that her own creation was funded by someone who wanted the investigation continued off the books. Emotional beat: horror curdling into fury at being made a tool, even a beloved one.

chapters.title: The Truce Clock
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Fleet dispatch announces the Meridian truce expires in forty days; after that, archives reopen and so do weapons bays. Isandro argues they have a deadline; Ines realizes whoever erased the massacre will erase them next. Emotional beat: the story's engine ignites — a countdown begins.

chapters.title: Crew of the Coriander
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter, mostly Ines's POV. The ship's small crew — engineer Bao, medic Sefa, teenage pilot Junie — reveal they were salvagers who found the wrecked Coriander drifting and chose to finish its last voyage. Emotional beat: wary strangers becoming something like a crew, the found-family theme taking root.

chapters.title: The Archive That Lies
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. At a neutral trade station, Ines queries the fleet archive using her original's credentials and watches the record rewrite itself in real time as she reads — an active erasure, not an old one. Someone knows she's looking. Emotional beat: paranoia; the enemy is present, patient, and institutional.

chapters.title: Admiral Voss
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. The architect of the cover-up, now a peacemaker celebrated for ending the war, reviews a report on Vesper-9 and orders a 'routine inspection.' We see his genuine belief that truth would kill a million people in a resumed war. Emotional beat: chilling sympathy for the antagonist.

chapters.title: Witnesses
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Following the manifest name backward, the crew finds a survivor of Calypso Reach living under a new identity — old woman Amaia, who has been silent for eleven years to keep her grandchildren safe. She agrees to testify only if Ines can guarantee the record will hold. Emotional beat: the cost of silence, and the courage of breaking it.

chapters.title: Inspection
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Voss's inspectors board Vesper-9 while the crew hides the Coriander in the beacon's shadow. Ines plays the dutiful clone, feeding the inspection team her original's authorized logs, lying with the dead woman's own voice. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into performance; Ines discovers she can deceive like her original could.

chapters.title: Junie's Frequency
chapters.summary: Junie's POV. The teenage pilot intercepts a coded fleet transmission and cracks part of it: Voss plans to scuttle the Coriander with all hands once the truce expires, closing the case permanently. Emotional beat: youthful recklessness maturing into responsibility; the crew becomes co-conspirators by choice.

chapters.title: The Original's Last Case Note
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Decrypted, her original's final note reveals she had identified Voss — and chose to have Ines created rather than go public, knowing the fleet monitored everything she touched. The clone was the dead woman's last move in a game she expected to lose. Emotional beat: devastating tenderness; Ines forgives being used because she was trusted.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Trade Station
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Returning for supplies, the crew is ambushed — someone sold their route. Bao takes a plasma burn covering Junie's escape; Isandro is captured. Ines learns the traitor was Amaia's grandson, coerced by fleet security. Emotional beat: the found family bleeds for the first time; trust survives the wound.

chapters.title: Interrogation
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Voss interrogates Isandro personally, offering him amnesty and erasure of his name in exchange for silence — the same bargain offered eleven years ago. Isandro refuses, telling Voss that a peace bought with three hundred corpses is just a slower massacre. Emotional beat: moral clarity under pressure; Isandro reclaims the name he's been running from.

chapters.title: Rescue Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The crew debates: rescue Isandro or use the remaining days to secure the archive evidence. Ines refuses the arithmetic — they do both, using the beacon itself as a jamming shield for a boarding run on the prison transport. Emotional beat: love against duty stated outright and chosen.

chapters.title: The Prison Transport
chapters.summary: Action chapter, rotating POV. The extraction nearly fails; Sefa is killed holding the docking clamp open. They pull Isandro out along with something unexpected: Voss's private log, seized by a guilt-ridden fleet archivist who smuggled it to the prisoners. Emotional beat: sacrifice, and the turn — they now hold undeniable proof.

chapters.title: Twenty-Nine Hours
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. With the truce expiring, the crew races to broadcast the full record — but the fleet network blocks all unauthorized transmissions. The only transmitter powerful enough, and forgotten enough, is Vesper-9's beacon. Emotional beat: desperate hope; the book's title pays off as the useless lighthouse becomes the weapon.

chapters.title: Signal
chapters.summary: Climax, ensemble POV. As Voss's ships close on Vesper-9, Ines broadcasts the massacre record on every frequency, wide-beam, unstoppable — while Junie flies the Coriander as a decoy and Bao holds the transmitter together by hand. Voss's own crews receive the truth mid-assault and refuse the firing order. Emotional beat: triumph earned through loss; the signal cannot be unheard.

chapters.title: Voss Falls
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Facing mutiny and an open archive, Voss surrenders rather than fire on his own fleet — insisting to the end that he bought peace with the only currency available. Ines, watching him taken into custody, feels no victory, only the weight of arithmetic done by other people. Emotional beat: ambiguous justice outside the law, exactly as promised.

chapters.title: Names on the Manifest
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The restored record lists all three hundred dead of Calypso Reach by name, and Isandro's name cleared at last. He chooses to leave — to carry testimony to the colonies — and Ines lets him go, understanding that some duties are chosen, not assigned. Emotional beat: bittersweet farewell; love honored by release.

chapters.title: The Light Stays On
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, epilogue. Months later, Vesper-9 is no longer forgotten: petitioners, historians, and survivors' kin arrive by the shuttle-load, and Bao and Junie stay on. Ines keeps the beacon burning, no longer maintaining a mystery but a memory. Final beat: the found family assembled around a signal that finally means what it says.
